mechanism: Bumetanide causes hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia which increases risk of QT prolongation; levofloxacin also has QT-prolonging potential, creating additive cardiac risk.
action: Monitor electrolytes (potassium and magnesium) regularly during concurrent use; obtain baseline and follow-up ECGs if QT interval is a concern; consider alternative antibiotic if patient has baseline electrolyte abnormalities or cardiac risk factors.
